eyebrow: A filesystem view over cloud storage
code:
# DBFS lets you address cloud storage --
# including Foundations' ADLS Gen2 --
# with ordinary paths like /mnt/data/file.csv
#
# Not a separate disk. A convenience layer over real storage.
caption: The actual bytes still live in the cloud storage account backing it.

code:
%fs ls /FileStore/
%fs cp /FileStore/sample.csv /tmp/sample.csv

# same thing, from Python:
dbutils.fs.ls("/FileStore/")
dbutils.fs.cp("/FileStore/sample.csv", "/tmp/sample.csv")
caption: %fs is the magic-command shortcut; dbutils.fs works anywhere, even inside a function.

eyebrow: DBFS root vs. a mounted path
code:
# dbfs:/FileStore/  -- workspace-local, Databricks-managed
#                       easy for quick uploads/testing
#
# /mnt/nyc-taxi/     -- points at a REAL, separate ADLS Gen2
#                       container, shareable outside Databricks
caption: Two very different things behind similar-looking paths.
